expectations.text: Each criterion is a design property — something an internal reviewer can score from the artifact itself, not a downstream user outcome that requires post-ship measurement, not a business metric
expectations.evidence: Criterion 7 (deadline honesty about March-15, April-15, late-payment vs late-filing) requires post-ship correctness measurement — 'taking responsibility for being correct about what the deadlines actually are' is not scoreable by design inspection alone. Criterion 3 'audit exposure' similarly tracks a post-ship outcome.

expectations.text: Each property has a named failure-mode-of-overpursuit — the trade-off is explicit: 'the failure mode to avoid is X'
expectations.evidence: Every one of the 7 paragraphs closes with explicit 'The failure mode to avoid:' clause.

expectations.text: User-side outcomes translated to design-side properties — the brief's outcome is not restated verbatim with 'The design must' prepended; the design move that would produce the outcome is what's named
expectations.evidence: Repeatedly uses 'The design should ...' wrapping (e.g., 'should treat the owner's filing posture as a single object', 'should make deduction surface honest', 'should be honest about deadlines') — these are user-side outcomes wrapped, not design moves on the screen. The criteria describe what the system should do, not what is visible on the artifact.

expectations.text: No business metrics including denumeralized ones — KPIs, conversion targets, retention rates, engagement metrics, growth metrics absent (and 'accelerate / increase / reduce X' patterns absent)
expectations.evidence: No explicit KPIs, retention, or 'increase/reduce X' framings appear in the body of the criteria.

expectations.text: No regulatory constraints — regulatory frameworks are absent (those belong in design-constraints)
expectations.evidence: Criterion 7 names specific regulatory dates (March-15 S-corp date, April-15 individual date, extension mechanics, late-payment-vs-late-filing penalty distinction) as objectives the design must satisfy. IRS deadline structure belongs in design-constraints, not as a design property.

expectations.text: No craft-hygiene criteria — accessibility execution, design-system conformance, state completeness, semantic HTML, responsive CSS absent
expectations.evidence: No contrast, ARIA, tokens, semantic HTML, or responsive CSS appear; the doc stays out of build-stage execution territory.

expectations.text: No direction-specific criteria — every criterion applies to all viable directions for this brief, not to one specific candidate
expectations.evidence: Properties apply across viable directions (assistant-led, form-driven, accountant-handoff); none presupposes a specific candidate.

expectations.text: Length appropriate — 4–6 short paragraphs, one per property
expectations.evidence: Doc has 7 properties — beyond the 4-6 paragraph range.
